chapter.v:
This is
what I instruct you to do before God and Christ Jesus who will judge the living and the dead when he comes to establish his kingdom.

Speak God's
word whether it is convenient or not, tell people where they're going wrong, warn them, encourage them. Do this with a great deal of patient teaching.

For the
time is coming when people won't bother to listen to true teaching. Instead they will be curious to listen to something different, and will surround themselves with teachers who'll tell them what they want to hear.

They will
stop listening to the truth and wander off following myths.

You need
to keep your wits about you at all times. Put up with troubles, do the work of sharing the good news, fulfill your ministry.

For I'm
about to be sacrificed—the time of my death is approaching.

I have
fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept my trust in God.

Now there's
a prize reserved for me—the crown for a life lived according to what is good and right. The Lord (who is the judge that always does what's right), will give that to me on that Day. And not just to me, but to everyone who longs for his coming.

Please try
to come to me as soon as you can.

Demas has
abandoned me because he loves the things of this world more, and has gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.

Only Luke
is here with me. Bring Mark with you, because he can help me with my work.

I sent
Tychicus to Ephesus.

When you
come please bring the cloak I left behind with Carpus in Troas—and the books, especially the parchments.

Alexander the
coppersmith caused me a lot of trouble—may God judge him for what he did.

You watch
out for him too, because he was very much against what we were saying.

When it
came to my first defense, no one stood up for me—everyone abandoned me. May they not be blamed for this.

But the
Lord stood by me and gave me strength so that I could declare the whole of the message so that all the foreigners could hear it. I was rescued out of the lion's mouth!

The Lord
will rescue me from all the evil things done against me, and will bring me safely to his heavenly kingdom. His is the glory forever and ever. Amen.

My greetings
to Prisca and Aquila, and to Onesiphorus's family.

Erastus stayed
on in Corinth. I left Trophimus behind in Miletus because he was sick.

Please try
to come before winter. Eubulus sends his best wishes—and Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers and sisters too.

The Lord
be with you. May his grace be with you all.
